# Draft:Gridware Cluster Scheduler

----
Gridware Cluster Scheduler (GCS) is a distributed resource management software system developed by HPC Gridware GmbH for high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) workloads. It serves as a commercial derivative and modernized successor to the Open Cluster Scheduler, an open-source cluster scheduling system based on Sun Grid Engine (SGE).
Background
The origins of the Gridware Cluster Scheduler date back to Sun Grid Engine, a distributed workload management system developed by Gridware GmbH and later acquired by Sun Microsystems in the late 1990s and early 2000s. After Sun Microsystems' acquisition, the product evolved under various commercial providers, including Oracle and subsequently Univa Corporation as Univa Grid Engine. In 2023, HPC Gridware GmbH initiated the Open Cluster Scheduler project as an open-source modernization effort built on the Sun Grid Engine software heritage, primarily updated to support contemporary hardware such as GPUs and other hardware accelerators important for HPC and AI workload.
Release and licensing
Gridware Cluster Scheduler version 9.0.0 was first officially released on October 14, 2024. While the Open Cluster Scheduler remains open-source under the Sun Industry Standards Source License (SISSL), the commercial Gridware Cluster Scheduler incorporates additional enterprise-oriented functionalities available under the Apache License 2.0.
Features
The Gridware Cluster Scheduler provides capabilities for scheduling, monitoring, and resource management, primarily tailored to enterprise computing environments running HPC, AI, and advanced computational workloads. The scheduler maintains broad compatibility with existing application integrations and standards, including Message Passing Interface (MPI) implementations and the Distributed Resource Management Application API (DRMAA). Compatibility with standard interfaces previously supported by Sun Grid Engine and Univa Grid Engine implementations is retained.
Key features introduced with the initial release include:
* UNIX group ID support for improved security and multi-user resource allocation.
* GPU resource management and enhanced performance accounting capabilities.
* API compatibility with DRMAA standards.
* Integration with HPC middleware platforms, including Nextflow from Seqera and NI SP EF Portal, successor of EnginFrame.
Use cases and applications
Common application areas and domains leveraging the Gridware Cluster Scheduler include academic research, electronic design automation (EDA), bioinformatics and life sciences, machine learning and artificial intelligence software ecosystems, engineering design simulation, as well as oil-and-gas exploration tasks demanding substantial computational resources.
Vendor support and documentation
HPC Gridware GmbH provides professional support for Gridware Cluster Scheduler, including technical assistance and consulting, regular feature updates, security patches, extensive documentation, and long-term software maintenance to ensure operational reliability within enterprise deployments.
